logp.method_description: The lipophilicity (log Po/w) was measured according to the literature method. Equal amounts of n-octanol and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) were thoroughly mixed in the oscillator for 24 hours. The mixture was then left to separate for a further 24 hours in order to obtain water and oil phase both which were saturated with the other. 1-3 were carefully dissolved in PBS (saturated with n-octanol) and obtained the saturated solution at room temperature (concentration denoted as Co). The saturated solution was then mixed with an equal amount of n-octanol (saturated with PBS) and shaken on oscillator for another 24 hours. After separation, the final concentration of1-3 in water phase as denoted as Cw. Both Co and Cw were measured by emission spectra area between 380-700 nm at the excitation light lex=350 nm. The lipophilicity of 1-3 was calculated according to the equation: log Po/w= log [(Co- Cw)/Cw].

To ensure complete saturation of the two phases, a mixture of 20 mL n-octanol and water (1:1 v/v) was vigorously shaken for 8 hours at a constant temperature using an oscillator. Following this, Ir-BPA and [Ir(ppy)2bpy]Cl (Ir-bpy) were introduced into a mixture of 1 mL water-saturated n-octanol and 1 mL n-octanol-saturated water to attain a final concentration of 20 μM. The solution was mixed and vortexed overnight on a constant temperature oscillator to guarantee maximum partitioning of the complexes into the respective phases. To determine the concentration of the complexes in each phase, the absorbance of the aqueous phase was measured at 265 nm after reaching a stationary phase. The LogP values were calculated using the following formula: LogP = log([Ir]octanol / [Ir]water). Where [Ir]octanol represented the concentration of Ir(III) complex in the n-octanol phase; and [Ir]water represented the concentration of Ir(III) complex in the water phase.

The octanol/water partition coefficient (Log P), is calculated based on the equation (1): Log P = Log(Coctanol / Cwater). The partition coefficient of complexes 1–7 were determined through the shake-flask method. To prepare water-saturated octanol, 4 mL of octanol was mixed with 1 ml of water and left for 24 h. Similarly, octanol-saturated water was prepared using the same procedure. The complex (50 μM) was then solubilized in 2 mL of saturated water by adding a minimal volume of DMSO, and this solution was added to 2 mL of saturated octanol. The resulting mixture underwent 24 h of shaking using a mechanical shaker, followed by settling and separation. The concentration of the complex was subsequently assessed through UV-vis absorption spectroscopy.
